## Intro

Many of the steps we have been discussing today are common to almost all software solutions available for the analysis of metabolomics data:

1. Commercial suites
2. Open source solutions which can be run locally (e.g. `xcms`, `mzmine`, `MS-DIAL`)
3. Freely available web services


## `xcms` on the web

### XCMS Online
Use `xcms` through a web interface

\weblink{https://xcmsonline.scripps.edu/landing_page.php?pgcontent=mainPage}{xcmsonline.scripps.edu}

### Workflow4Metabolomics (W4M)
Use `xcms` through Galaxy. The French metabolomics network (MetaboHUB) also provides tools for statistics, annotation and pathway analysis

\weblink{https://workflow4metabolomics.org/}{workflow4metabolomics.org}


## R based analysis

### MetaboAnalyst
Statistical, functional and integrative analysis of metabolomics data, linked to the Human Metabolome Database

\weblink{https://www.metaboanalyst.ca/}{metaboanalyst.ca}


## Without R

### OpenMS (C++ and Python)
Open-source C++ library (with Python bindings) for LC/MS data management and analysis, part of the de.NBI Center for integrative Bioinformatics

\weblink{https://www.openms.de/}{openms.de}

### KNIME
Open source platform for creating data science workflows; it also runs OpenMS tools

\weblink{https://www.knime.com/}{knime.com}


## Human Friendly Open Solutions

### mzmine 4
Mass-spectrometry data processing for LC-MS, GC-MS, ion mobility and MS imaging; free for academic use, licensed for commercial use

\weblink{https://mzio.io/mzmine/}{mzio.io/mzmine}

### MS-DIAL
Universal program for untargeted metabolomics: multiple instruments (GC/MS, GC/MS/MS, LC/MS, LC/MS/MS) and MS vendors (Agilent, Bruker, LECO, Sciex, Shimadzu, Thermo, Waters)

\weblink{https://systemsomicslab.github.io/compms/msdial/main.html}{systemsomicslab.github.io/compms/msdial}
